first_step_test: A beginner can place one pointed left post and two light rail edges at their final positions; the blank interiors keep the first job to a connected gate corner.

source.notes: Owner-directed gate correction: built-in raster image editing produced a revised six-panel contact sheet from the original gate artwork. The original high-fidelity early sheet and all six old JPG masters are preserved privately under rejected-progressions. The current saved sequence starts with light construction, adds slats and brace, then introduces weathered grain and hardware before ground details and restrained color.

frames.visible_job: Lightly outline the pointed left post and one connected top rail at their final positions, with a small base grass mark.
frames.instruction: With light HB pressure, draw the tall left post and its pointed cap. From the upper third, pull two level lines to the right for the top rail, leaving its far end open. Add a tiny grass tuft at the post base; leave the wood interiors blank.

frames.visible_job: Outline the matching right post and lower rail, keeping both posts and rails lightly drawn and untextured.
frames.instruction: At the open top-rail end, lightly outline a matching right post and pointed cap. Link the posts with two low level lines for the bottom rail, then add a tiny right-base grass tuft. Keep the wood blank for now.

frames.visible_job: Place exactly three slats between the rails and one diagonal brace behind them, with only faint grain suggestions.
frames.instruction: Between the rails, draw exactly three evenly spaced upright slats. Draw one rising diagonal brace from lower left to upper right, stopping its edges whenever a slat covers it. Add only a few faint grain strokes along the new boards.

frames.visible_job: Add two hinges and one latch, then develop the weathered graphite grain and knots on the established wood.
frames.instruction: At the left post, draw one iron hinge beside each rail. Add one short latch across the upper-right join. Follow the length of the established posts, rails, slats, and brace with uneven graphite grain and a few knots; keep every contour and overlap fixed.

frames.visible_job: Set three uneven path stones, enlarge the two established grass tufts, and add a broken ground shadow.
frames.instruction: Draw three flattened stones below the bottom rail. Enlarge the small grass tuft at each outer post base, then add a short broken shadow beneath the gate.

final_step.visible_job: Deepen established contours and add restrained brown-gray colored pencil over the existing gate, hardware, stones, grass, and shadow.
final_step.instruction: Strengthen selected graphite edges; shade the established rails, posts, and slats with pale warm brown, the hinges and latch cool gray, and the stones and grass lightly. Leave paper gaps for weathered wood.
adds: graphite shading and restrained color on established regions

visual_review.first_step_observation: The saved first JPG contains one pale pointed left post, an attached open-ended upper rail, and a tiny left-base grass mark. Blank wood interiors and light graphite contours make its height, width, and connection copyable before texture is attempted.
visual_review.draw_through_observation: I reviewed the revised full six-panel sheet and all five adjacent saved-JPG pairs. Left and right post bases, the two rail heights, exactly three slats, the rising brace behind them, two left hinges, the right latch, three path stones, and both grass bases stay at their intended anchors. Step 4 visibly adds the deferred wood grain; the finish colors established contours only. No temporary guides were used or removed.

transitions.observed_addition: The pale left post, pointed cap, open-ended top rail, and tiny left-base grass remain. A matching pointed right post joins the rail end; two lower horizontal edges connect the posts, and a tiny right-base grass mark appears. Both wood interiors stay blank.
transitions.instruction_match: Step 2 tells the reader to attach the right post at the open rail end and draw the low two-line rail with light pressure; the saved crop shows those strokes and no premature grain.

transitions.observed_addition: The two posts and two rails retain their corners and blank interiors. Exactly three upright slats appear between the rails. One brace rises lower-left to upper-right behind them, visible only in the four gaps, with a few faint lengthwise grain suggestions.
transitions.instruction_match: Step 3 calls for three spaced slats, a brace stopped at every foreground slat, and only faint grain; those are the visible additions, with the established rail and post anchors still clear.

transitions.observed_addition: The three slats remain in separate slots and the rising brace remains behind them. One upper and one lower hinge attach to the left post at rail heights; the latch crosses the upper-right join. Uneven grain and a few knots now darken the existing posts, rails, slats, and brace.
transitions.instruction_match: Step 4 explicitly places both hinges, the right latch, and the deferred graphite grain; the darker wood is now taught rather than appearing in Step 1. No structural board is added or removed.

transitions.observed_addition: Both pointed posts, two rails, three slats, rear brace, two hinges, and latch retain their attachments. The existing base grass grows beside each post. Three flattened stones appear in front of the gate in receding order, with broken graphite ground shading beneath.
transitions.instruction_match: Step 5 asks for three flat path stones, larger grass from the two existing tufts, and a broken shadow; the saved crop adds those ground marks while keeping the gate fixed.

transitions.observed_addition: The same two posts, rails, three slats, rear brace, two hinges, latch, three stones, enlarged base grass, and broken ground shadow remain. Warm brown shades existing wood, cool gray shades iron and stones, and muted green follows the established grass.
transitions.instruction_match: The final instruction calls for restrained color and selected graphite emphasis on the already drawn wood, hardware, stones, grass, and shadow. No new structural contour or prop appears in the saved finish.
